answer: Last spring, one script farmed 2,000 accounts. Every account climbed the same copper trellis of starter tasks in identical order and hours. Payout reads the shape of each climb: curves over 92 percent alike are paid as one identity. A real pearl layers unevenly under a lens; his lines ran parallel, so the farm earned a single share. Beating it means maintaining a different script per account, and lazy variants still cluster. Honest cost: newcomers sharing a tutorial look alike early, so young curves are matched loosely at first.
